results.claim: There is an explicit packing of 518 A10 rectangles in one A1 rectangle.
results.proof_sketch: Use container [0,594]×[0,841]. Place A_{i,j}=[37i,37(i+1)]×[26j,26(j+1)] for 0≤i<2, 0≤j<32 (64 rectangles). Place B_i=[74+37i,74+37(i+1)]×[0,26] for 0≤i<14 (14 rectangles). Finally place C_{i,j}=[74+26i,74+26(i+1)]×[26+37j,26+37(j+1)] for 0≤i<20, 0≤j<22 (440 rectangles). The three families occupy respectively [0,74]×[0,832], [74,592]×[0,26], and [74,594]×[26,840], so they are contained and have disjoint interiors. Their total size is 64+14+440=518.

results.claim: No packing can contain 519 A10 rectangles; a ten-residue periodic marker certificate gives the upper bound 518.
results.proof_sketch:
First, arbitrary-real-coordinate packings reduce to integer-coordinate packings. With vertical coordinates and orientations fixed, minimize the sum of horizontal coordinates over the nonempty compact feasible set. Every rectangle not at x=0 then has an immediate left blocker; otherwise it could move slightly left. Following blockers strictly decreases x and ends at x=0, expressing every x-coordinate as a sum of integer widths. Fix these integral horizontal coordinates and analogously minimize the sum of vertical coordinates, yielding integral y-coordinates.

Now mark unit cell (x,y) when (x mod 37,y mod 37) belongs to P={(3,3),(7,25),(10,14),(14,7),(18,29),(22,11),(25,33),(29,22),(33,36),(36,18)}. Let X and Y be the respective coordinate-residue sets. In each cyclically ordered set, every four successive elements have first-to-fourth cyclic distance at least 11. Hence an 11-residue interval contains at most three selected residues, so its complementary 26-residue interval contains at least seven. A 37×26 rectangle therefore contains at least seven marks using Y, and a 26×37 rectangle contains at least seven using X.

Among the 594 columns, residues 0 and 1 occur 17 times and all others 16 times; X excludes 0 and 1. Among the 841 rows, residues 0 through 26 occur 23 times and the rest 22 times; seven elements of Y are in the first group and three in the second. Thus the container has exactly 16(7·23+3·22)=3632 marks. Disjoint rectangles cover disjoint unit cells, whereas 519 rectangles would require at least 7·519=3633 marks. Therefore every packing has at most 518 rectangles.

final_writeup:
The recorded 258-versus-259 dichotomy is false for the literal ISO sizes supplied in the input. An A10 sheet is 26×37 mm and an A1 sheet is 594×841 mm; their exact orthogonal packing number is

OPT(594,841,37,26)=518.

A checkable lower-bound construction divides the container into three occupied blocks. The left block [0,74]×[0,832] is tiled by a 2×32 grid of 37×26 rectangles. The upper-right block [74,592]×[0,26] contains fourteen 37×26 rectangles. The lower-right block [74,594]×[26,840] is tiled by a 20×22 grid of 26×37 rectangles. These give 64+14+440=518 nonoverlapping sheets.

For the upper bound, use the ten residue pairs
P={(3,3),(7,25),(10,14),(14,7),(18,29),(22,11),(25,33),(29,22),(33,36),(36,18)} modulo 37, marking every unit cell with one of these residue pairs. Every cyclic interval of 26 residues contains at least seven of the first-coordinate residues and at least seven of the second-coordinate residues. Consequently every integer-positioned A10 rectangle, in either orientation, contains at least seven marked cells. The entire A1 container contains exactly

16(7·23+3·22)=3632

marked cells. Thus a packing of 519 sheets would require at least 7·519=3633 distinct marked cells, which is impossible.

This also covers arbitrary real placements. Holding vertical coordinates fixed, minimize the sum of horizontal coordinates over the compact feasible set. Every rectangle not touching x=0 must then have an immediate left blocker. A finite blocker chain reaches x=0, so each horizontal coordinate is a sum of widths 26 and 37 and is integral. Holding those horizontal coordinates fixed and applying the same argument vertically makes all vertical coordinates integral without changing the packing cardinality.

Therefore the maximum is 518, so neither 258 nor 259 is correct for A10-in-A1. The construction and marker certificate fully resolve the literal target.
